title: embeddings-rerank-dim-mismatch-scratch
content:
Quick scratchpad for the embeddings->rerank endpoint weirdness (dim mismatch errors + occasional latency spikes).

Context:
- Reported by search team on 2026-02-27: rerank job failing ~2-3% of requests with 'embedding dimension mismatch' and some requests showing 5-10s tail latency spikes.
- Endpoint: /v1/embeddings/rerank (internal), uses model: openclip-bridge-v2 (384 dim) -> reranker model expects 768 dim (legacy config?), or we quantize/concatenate? uncertain.
- Affects both hosted and dedicated; Private not reported yet.

Observations so far:
- Error sample from logs (2026-02-27T18:12:03Z):
  ERROR rerank.service - embedding_apply failed: DimensionMismatch: expected 768, got 384 (vector length 384)
  request_id=rq_0a1b2c3d
- Most successes show embeddings length 384. Failures always show 384->expected 768 mismatch.
- Latency spikes correlate with requests that hit fallback reranker (we fall back to legacy rerank for unknown model), but not 1:1. Some 384-dim requests succeed quickly (20-50ms).
- Canary rollout: new embedding backend (embedder v2) rolled to 10% on 2026-02-25. Hypothesis: some clients still sending 768-dim embeddings (old embedder), some sending 384, and our rerank routing sometimes mismatches the reranker variant. But logs show expected=768 but got 384 (so server expected 768). Which side sets expected dimension? either we pick reranker model variant based on request metadata or based on model selector which might mis-route.

Commands/queries tried:
- Reproduced locally with curl against staging-rerank:
  curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/re-rank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOK' -d '{"query_embedding": [0.1, ... (384 floats) ...], "candidate_embeddings": [[...]] }'
  -> 400 DimensionMismatch: expected 768, got 384

- Quick python test:
  from requests import post
  payload = {"query_embedding": [0.0]*384, "candidates": [[0.0]*384]*5}
  r = post("https://staging.internal/embeddings/rerank", json=payload)
  print(r.status_code, r.text)
  -> consistent 400 on staging-rerank, but on dev-rerank (local) same payload returns 200 (score list).

- Looked at routing logic in 'rerank-router' (commit d4f8):
  - Router reads request.meta['embedding_schema'] or inspects first embedding length to pick reranker variant.
  - There's a race: if request.meta is missing, router uses default_reranker which is currently set to 'rerank-v1-768' in prod config.
  - On canary rollout we flipped default to v1-768 by mistake when embedder v2 (384) rolled. Should be default v1-384.

Latency spike investigation:
- Correlation between errors and latency: some requests (no error) still have 3-8s latency. Stack traces show: waiting on model AGRPC call timed out, then fallback to CPU reranker which is slow.
- Logs: 2026-02-27T18:21:11Z request_id=rq_9z8y7x -> initial reranker call timed out after 1500ms -> fallback invoked -> total 6123ms.
- Hypothesis: fallback path is synchronous and uses CPU scoring loop; when fallback queue grows, tail latency increases.

Hypotheses summary:
1) Dimension mismatch: config/regression where default_reranker variant expects 768 while embedder switched to 384. Router isn't reliably inspecting embedding length when meta missing.
2) Latency spikes: triggered when primary reranker times out (network/GRPC or model overloaded) and synchronous CPU fallback is used; fallback path not scaled/async, causing long tails.
3) Some clients/ingest pipelines may still submit 768-dim embeddings; mixed dimensions require deterministic routing or runtime validation and early reject with helpful error.

Immediate next steps / TODOs (short):
- [ ] Hotfix router: change default_reranker to v1-384 on staging/prod until canary completes OR make router inspect first embedding length before routing. (quick patch in rerank-router service)
- [ ] Add runtime validation on API layer: if embedding length not in allowed set (384|768) return 400 with explicit message and hint which model expected. Safer than silent misrouting.
- [ ] Instrument metrics: add counter for dimension_mismatch, fallback_invoked, primary_timeout_ms, fallback_latency_histogram. Add dashboard for 95/99p latencies per reranker variant.
- [ ] Scale fallback pool / make fallback path async: push scoring to background worker so main request can stream partial results or return error earlier. Short-term increase CPU workers.
- [ ] Run data scan on last 24h to measure distribution of embedding dims by client-id; annotate client owners and roll back/coordinate embedder rollout.
- [ ] Postmortem/incident blurb for CS+search team explaining root cause & mitigation plan.

Notes/commands to deploy patches quickly:
- Change default in config-service: POST /v1/configs/rerank/default -> {"default_reranker": "rerank-v1-384"}
- Quick router patch (python): (in rerank-router/main.py)
  if 'embedding_schema' not in meta:
      dim = len(request.json()["query_embedding"])
      if dim == 384: route_to = 'rerank-v1-384'
      elif dim == 768: route_to = 'rerank-v1-768'
      else: return 400, 'unsupported embedding dim'

- Local repro dataset: saved as /tmp/repro-embeddings-2026-02-27.json (sample of failed requests).

Error snippets saved:
- "DimensionMismatch: expected 768, got 384 (vector length 384)"
- "PrimaryRerankerTimeout: grpc call exceeded 1500ms"
- "FallbackScoringQueueLength=42, processing_time_ms=5200"

Who to ping:
- @Maya Patel (applied-ml) - for embedder rollout history
- @Aran Singh (serving-runtime) - for router behavior + config-service
- @SRE on-call - for tail latency and autoscale checks

Misc thoughts / long-term fixes:
- Add a small embedding header: {"schema": "clip-v2-384"} to make routing deterministic and future-proof. Avoid implicit defaulting.
- Introduce a typed contract for embedding-producing models and a registry (model -> output-dim) that router consults. Config flips only via canary process.
- Make fallback scoring async + streaming: return partial ranked top-k if fallback slower than X ms, or degrade gracefully with approximate scoring.

Open questions:
- Did any clients explicitly request reranker variant via header? (search team says no)
- Are there any proxies/load-balancers that could be mutating request bodies and dropping metadata? Need to check API gateway logs.
- Why do some 384-dim requests succeed even with default=768? Maybe they include meta or hit a different router instance with different config. Need to correlate router instance id in logs.

Immediate next action (today):
1) push router config change on staging to route by embedding length; test with bulk repro.
2) add temporary metric 'embedding_length_received' and alert if unexpected dims > 0.
3) prepare rollback plan for embedder rollout if client owners show mismatch.

-- Evelyn

Notes to self: keep this doc light, move to confluence postmortem template after incident wrap-up.
